author: reek
body: The LwM2M Object 5 firmware update, end to end, with nothing faked except the socket.

author: reek
body: The image is a REAL signed CDX built by cdx-encode-signed, not a byte pattern -- so the magic, the header, the capability manifest and the Ed25519 signature are all the genuine article. It is chunked into REAL CoAP Block2 responses built by coap-build-request. The client parses them, stages every block into the flash bank through the Flash effect, and Gate A hashes the BANK. Gate B is the real five-phase verifier via evaluate-load, against a real trust lattice and policy.

author: reek
body: What is not real is the UDP socket: codex-vm serves only DNS on UDP and drops everything else, so no guest can complete a live CoAP exchange at all. The responses are handed to the client directly. Every inch above the socket is exercised.

author: reek
body: The second half is the design's first adversarial scenario. One byte is flipped in transit. The signature is still the publisher's, the blocks still arrive in order, the CoAP is still well-formed -- and the staged image must be refused, because Gate A hashes what landed in the bank rather than what the client thinks it sent. The device must end on Result 5 (integrity) with the old firmware still the one that boots.

author: reek
body: A small but genuine signed firmware CDX. It declares Console so the manifest carries a real capability the verifier can weigh.

author: reek
body: A CoAP server, in the shape the client will meet one: 2.05 Content with a Block2 option, more set on every block but the last.

author: reek
body: szx 2 is 64-byte blocks: block size is two raised to szx plus four.

author: reek
body: One byte flipped in transit, in the middle of the image. The publisher's signature is untouched and every block is well-formed CoAP in the right order.
